messages:
Maya Chen: FYI escalation from ACME: they see intermittent 429s but their org quota looks fine. they say only a single project and key in use. hitting from a proxy pool (mobile carriers) — wondering if IP-based limits are clashing with API-key/project limits. attaching headers from one failure.

Samir Patel: can you paste the raw response headers + the exact curl used? most of the time the Retry-After / X-RateLimit-* headers tell us which limiter fired.

Maya Chen: pasted below (redacted keys):
```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 14 Nov 2025 18:12:01 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 163
Retry-After: 30
x-redwood-limiter: ip_rate_limit_v2
{
  "error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"IP rate limit exceeded"}
}
```

Maya Chen: customer says they never hit per-key limit; their dashboard shows project usage far under project quota.

Eli Torres: ok `x-redwood-limiter: ip_rate_limit_v2` is clear — the edge has a per-IP bucket. when a lot of clients share NAT/proxy you can exceed that even if each key is under quota.

Ops Oncall: adding context — we have three layers: org-level quota (monthly commit), project/api-key per-minute quotas, and edge IP-based abusive protection. IP limiter lives in CDN layer and is configured to protect against noisy carrier IPs. It can return 429 with `x-redwood-limiter` set.

Samir Patel: steps to repro and triage for support engineer: 1) get a failing request sample (headers shown). 2) check internal rate-limit dashboard for that IP (internal tool: https://internal.redwood/rl/dashboard) with `ip=1.2.3.4` (customer-provided IP). 3) check key-level usage: `rbx-internal get-usage --key sk-prod-REDACTED --window 1m` 4) check org billing state: `billing status --org acme-corp`.

Maya Chen: customer provided flow: their mobile SDK pools client requests through a handful of carrier IPs; spikes during batch syncs. they've already tried retry with exponential backoff but still see repeated 429s for a subset of users.

Eli Torres: suggestions: short-term: 1) ask them to include `X-Forwarded-For` with client IP (if their proxy can pass it) — our edge will prefer XFF for IP bucketing if trusted. 2) issue a temporary increase for that org's IP threshold (support action). 3) advise them to rotate to per-user API keys or per-device keys to spread per-key quotas if possible.

Support Bot: support ticket #INC-20251114-87 created and linked to org: acme-corp. SLA: respond within 2h.

Samir Patel: clarification on limit semantics we should give customer: - org quota is monthly (tokens) and affects billing/consumption, not immediate 429s. - project/api-key quotas are enforced per-key and are the usual source of 429 for sustained high throughput. - IP limits are separate and applied before key-level in the CDN/edge to protect platform integrity.

Maya Chen: customer asks: if we rotate keys will it avoid IP-based 429s?

Eli Torres: no — rotating keys won't change IP bucket behavior. If the traffic funnels through the same set of source IPs the ip_rate_limit will still apply. Key rotation only helps if they hit per-key quotas.

Maya Chen: customer also reported one-off 401s when they rotated keys and used an old cached token — any auth edge cases to warn them about?

Samir Patel: yes: common pitfalls: - cached ~/.redwood_token or env var in worker not updated -> 401 or 403. - mixing org-scoped keys and project-scoped keys: some endpoints require project header `X-Project-ID` when key is project-limited. - clock skew for signed short-lived tokens causes auth fails. advise them to check error body exactly: `{"type":"authentication_error","message":"token_revoked"}` etc.

Maya Chen: reproduced 401 sample: `{"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"token_revoked","hint":"use new key"}}`

Ops Oncall: for mitigation we can: - whitelist specific known carrier IP ranges for a limited window (requires SRE approval) - enable trusted XFF for customer's proxy so edge uses client IP not proxy IP - temporarily bump ip limiter for that org/project (we have a soft quota override path for escalations).

Samir Patel: repro plan for support engineer to run with customer: 1) capture exact failing request with `curl -v` including source IP observed. 2) ask them to try a control test from a non-proxied network (home wifi or tether) to confirm it's IP-bound. 3) run `internal rl lookup --ip 1.2.3.4` + `internal rl lookup --key sk-prod-REDACTED` and paste screenshots/links. 4) if IP shows saturated, propose trusted-XFF or temporary override.

Maya Chen: the customer has compliance constraints so they can't expose client IPs in logs publicly — asked if we can accept a hashed IP to look it up.

Eli Torres: we can accept sha256(ip) in the internal tool and map it if they share the salt, but easier is they share the /32 or /24 range of the carrier. we can then check recent hits.

BillingBot: org acme-corp payment status: active; no billing blocks. monthly committed tokens: 5M; consumed: 400k (8%).

Samir Patel: next action list: - Maya: request carrier IP ranges + attempts timestamps + example curl with headers. - I'll run ip lookup and key usage, and if ip limiter misfire we request SRE whitelist for 2h. - Eli: prepare internal playbook snippet for support for IP vs key 429 troubleshooting so we can reuse.

Maya Chen: noted and sent customer the repro checklist + temporary backoff advice (50ms jittered exponential starting 100ms) and link to doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/rate-limits#ip-vs-key. they appreciate the triage, keeping ticket open. :thumbsup:

Ops Oncall: pinging SRE if we need a rapid whitelist: @ops-sre — can we preapprove a 2h ip_limit relaxation for org acme-corp if I file emergency request?

(Ops Oncall adds reaction :eyes:)

Support Bot: updated ticket INC-20251114-87 with Samir notes and attached ip-lookup request.

Maya Chen: will update thread after SRE reply and customer tests.
